title: Defect register
description: Candidate and confirmed product defects for one project. A failing test is not a defect: this record is what justifies calling it one. Never write a credential, token, secret or unnecessary PII into any field here.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601. Date, or date-time. Length alone is not a date.

title.description: Must identify the failure, not the area. Good: Customer creation accepts duplicate email despite uniqueness validation. Rejected: Customer issue, Test failed, Page not working.

summary.description: Fuller prose description where the title cannot carry it.

state.description: Predicted risk is not a defect and a failure is not automatically a defect. Only CONFIRMED_DEFECT asserts a real product fault, and it requires confirmation.product_cause_established true.

discovery_method.description: How this was found. Not every defect comes from a failing test, and defects found only by exploratory testing are the ones a suite would never have caught. SILENT_FAILURE_DETECTION and CROSS_LAYER_CHECK matter most: a backend failure behind a successful-looking UI is invisible to any test that only asserts the UI.

failure_class.description: CLAUDE.md section 9 class of the originating failure. Required in practice when discovery_method is AUTOMATED_TEST. State CONFIRMED_DEFECT alongside a non-product failure_class is a contradiction.

confirmation.description: The confirmation protocol. Absent or unevidenced confirmation caps state at POTENTIAL_DEFECT.

expected_behaviour_source.description: The oracle. Requirement id, business rule id, API contract, accessibility standard or security policy that establishes what SHOULD happen. The code does X therefore X is correct is not a source.

non_product_causes_ruled_out.description: Which of automation, environment, test data, network, dependency and configuration were eliminated, and how.

product_evidence.description: What in the product was inspected: endpoint response, DOM, log, source location.

duplicate_decision.description: Outcome of the duplicate search. Never create a duplicate defect.

searched.description: Where you looked: knowledge/defects/, this register, the external tracker, prior run reports.

severity_rationale.description: Impact-based justification: business impact, user impact, workflow blockage, financial, security, accessibility, data corruption, affected population, workaround availability, compliance.

priority_recommendation.description: A recommendation only. Priority is business-owned; QA does not assign organizational priority.

role.description: The actor or permission level the defect occurs under, where it matters.

steps.description: Reproduction steps, specific enough for someone else to follow without this session's context.

test_data_ref.description: Path or identifier of the data used. Never the data itself when it carries PII.

evidence.description: Project-relative paths: screenshot, video, trace, log, console output, HAR, request and response capture.

test_refs.description: Project-relative test file paths, and the execution that produced the failure.

regression_decision.description: Every confirmed defect triggers this decision. Do not reflexively add one UI regression test per bug: fix the underlying quality gap and prefer the lowest layer that detects it reliably.

fix_validation.description: Three levels. Rerunning only the originally failing test is not fix validation.

status.description: QA does not close a defect unless explicitly authorised to. FIX_VERIFIED is the terminal QA state by default.

at.description: ISO-8601. Date, or date-time. Length alone is not a date.

external.description: Populated only when an authorised defect tracker integration exists. Absent means the defect lives in this register alone.

discovered_at.description: ISO-8601. Date, or date-time. Length alone is not a date.

cross_layer.description: Evidence from each layer of truth, for defects where UI appearance and backend reality diverge. Populate for high-risk workflows and for every suspected silent failure.

ui.description: What the interface showed the user.

api.description: Status codes and response bodies actually returned.

events.description: Events produced or not produced, and whether consumers acted.

logs.description: Backend errors, including ones the UI never surfaced.

correlation_id.description: The single most useful field for tying layers together. Ask for it as an OBSERVABILITY_GAP where it does not exist.

consistent.description: False means the layers disagree, which is itself the defect.

divergence.description: Where and how the layers disagreed. "UI showed Transfer complete; API returned 500; no ledger row written" is the shape of this field.

silent.description: True when the product reported success, or reported nothing, while failing. These never surface as a red test and are found only by looking past the UI.

scope.description: What was actually run: test ids, layer, or the selected impact set.

evidence.description: Command run and its real result. Should pass is not a result.

at.description: ISO-8601. Date, or date-time. Length alone is not a date.
